info.title: kube-wl-ai API
info.description: Kubernetes GPU resource scheduling and management system

get.description: Returns 200 as soon as the process is serving requests.
Checks dependencies that must be reachable before serving traffic.

Public keys Grafana uses to validate monitoring tokens.

Contains nothing secret; with HMAC signing the set is empty and Grafana is
configured with the shared secret instead.

post.summary: Log in and start a session
post.description:
Verify credentials against the configured providers and issue a session.

The access token is returned in the body; the refresh token is set as an
httpOnly cookie and never appears in the response payload.

The attempt is rate limited *before* the credentials are checked — see
`app.auth.rate_limit` — so a locked-out attempt costs no directory round trip
and cannot be used to make the LDAP server do work.

post.summary: Rotate the refresh token and issue a new access token
post.description:
Exchange the refresh cookie for a new session.

Rotation is unconditional: the presented token is revoked and replaced. If a
token that was already rotated is presented again, the whole family is
revoked — that is the standard defence against a stolen refresh token.

401.description: Refresh token missing, expired or already used

post.description:
Revoke the presented refresh token and clear the cookie.

Deliberately does not require a valid access token: a session whose access
token has already expired must still be able to log out cleanly.

The caller's own workspace.

A dedicated endpoint because a user belongs to exactly one workspace and the
UI needs it on every page load; listing and filtering would be wasteful and
would depend on the scope filter getting the single-row case right.

Re-apply the namespace, quota, limit range and network policy.

Idempotent by design: this is the repair action for a workspace stuck in
``error``, and the same call the periodic reconcile loop makes.

post.description:
Assign a user.

A user may belong to exactly one workspace, so assigning someone who already
has one requires ``moveFromExisting: true`` — silently relocating their
files and running workloads would be a data-loss bug.

delete.description:
Revoke a grant.

The quota shrinks immediately. Running workloads are deliberately left
alone — Kubernetes will refuse new pods but will not kill what is running,
which is the behaviour an administrator wants when draining a pool.

schema.title: Response List Ssh Keys Api V1 Ssh Keys Get

post.description:
Register a public key.

Only the public half ever reaches the platform; it is mounted into instances
as ``authorized_keys``. The fingerprint is computed from the key material,
so the same key cannot be registered twice under different names.

Validation (ownership, pool grant, quota) happens before anything reaches

get.description:
Container logs.

``previous=true`` reads the terminated container's output, which is the only

get.description:
Mint the short-lived ticket that opens the instance's web IDE.

The ticket is scoped to this instance and namespace and expires in minutes,
so a URL pasted into a chat becomes useless almost immediately. It is a
distinct token *type*, so it can never be used as an API credential.

delete.description:
Retire an application from the catalogue.

A PATCH-shaped operation behind DELETE because the row is kept: instances
created from it reference it, and those references must stay resolvable.

post.description:
Create an instance from this application.

Requires ``instance:create`` rather than an application permission: the
result is an instance, and it is bounded by exactly the same rules.

Returns the row rather than 204: it is retired rather than erased, and the

post.description:
Refresh the catalogue from the registry.

Deliberately not a ``GET``: it writes, and a request that mutates state must

get.description: Headline totals for the window, plus the caller's own share of them.
One point per day, with empty days present as zeros.
Totals grouped by user, group, workspace, accelerator or workload kind.
Filter vocabulary, so the client's controls cannot drift from the API.
Download the window as CSV, one row per day and workload bucket.

post.description:
Recompute the daily rollup for a window.

Always available to a global administrator, and run on a schedule besides.
Both ranges are optional; omitting them recomputes the default lookback,
which is what an operator wants after noticing today's number looks wrong.

get.description:
The caller's own tokens. Returns a bare list, like the other small
catalogues, because a person has a handful of tokens and never pages them.

schema.title: Response List Api Tokens Api V1 Api Tokens Get

post.description:
Mint a token and return it **once**.

The response is the only time the secret exists in a readable form. A client
that loses it revokes the token and makes another — which is a better
outcome than a system that can reproduce secrets on demand.

Scopes are validated against what the caller holds right now, so a token can
never be created naming a permission its owner lacks. A token created *by*
another token is further limited to that token's own scopes, so a credential
cannot mint a successor with more authority than itself.

delete.summary: Revoke one of the caller's API tokens
delete.description:
Revoke a token by id.

Revocation is immediate and total: the row is deleted, so the next request
presenting the credential fails to resolve it. Out-of-scope ids are a 404
rather than a 403 — token ids are sequential, and a 403 would confirm that
somebody else's token exists.

get.summary: List audit entries visible to the caller
get.description:
Newest first, always.

`requestId` is the filter that turns this from a browsing screen into a
diagnostic one: every log line the application emitted while handling a
request carries the same id, so one value ties the audit row to the trace.

get.summary: Filter options available within the caller's scope
get.description:
The values the filter controls should offer.

Derived from scoped rows rather than from the permission catalogue: offering
an action that nobody in the caller's scope has performed would disclose that
the action exists elsewhere.

The same rows as the listing, without the page bound, as CSV.

It reuses `AuditFilters` and therefore the same scoped statement as the
listing. That is not a convenience: an export assembled separately from the
listing eventually gets assembled *differently*, and on this table the
difference is handing somebody rows they cannot see on screen.

When the row ceiling truncates the result, the file says so in its own last
line. A CSV that stops early while claiming a date range is the one artefact
most likely to end up in an incident report unexamined.

get.summary: 监控总览（含已签名的 Grafana 面板地址）
get.description: Inventory, the caller's live containers, and signed panel URLs.

post.summary: 重新签发某个面板的短期地址
post.description:
Mint a fresh URL for one dashboard.

A `POST` because it creates a credential — it is not safe to retry blindly
from a cache, and the method says so. The permission is checked against the
*dashboard*, not merely against monitoring in general: holding
`monitor:read_self` must not produce a fleet-wide URL by naming its key.

ApiMessage.title: ApiMessage
ApiMessage.description: A plain confirmation payload for endpoints with nothing else to return.

ApiTokenCreate.title: ApiTokenCreate
ApiTokenCreate.description: Request body for minting a token.

ApiTokenIssued.title: ApiTokenIssued
ApiTokenIssued.description: A freshly minted token, with the one and only sight of the secret.

ApiTokenRead.title: ApiTokenRead
ApiTokenRead.description:
A token as it may be shown after creation.

There is no ``token`` field here and there must never be one: the secret is
returned exactly once, by `ApiTokenIssued`, and is not recoverable. Anything
that could render a stored token would mean we had stored it.

ApplicationCategory.title: ApplicationCategory
ApplicationCategory.description:
A coarse grouping for the application catalogue.

Deliberately short. A long taxonomy decays into "other" the moment nobody
curates it, and the search box is what people actually use.

ApplicationDetail.title: ApplicationDetail
ApplicationDetail.description: The catalogue card plus the introduction and the launch defaults.

ApplicationLaunch.title: ApplicationLaunch
ApplicationLaunch.description:
Launch an application as an instance in the caller's workspace.

Every field is optional and falls back to the application's default, so the
common case is a bare ``{}``.

ApplicationVisibility.title: ApplicationVisibility
ApplicationVisibility.description:
Who may see and launch an application.

Widening is deliberate and explicit: a private definition is the author's
scratch space, ``workspace`` shares it with colleagues in the same
namespace, ``group`` with the whole lab, and ``global`` with the university.

AuditLogRead.title: AuditLogRead
AuditLogRead.description:
One audit row.

``actorUsername`` is read from the denormalised column rather than from the
relationship: it is the value recorded *at the time*, and a user renamed
since then must not retroactively rewrite history.

AuditMeta.title: AuditMeta
AuditMeta.description:
What the filter controls should offer.

Every list is built within the caller's scope, so a group administrator is
not shown a value that only exists in somebody else's history.

DataScopeResponse.title: DataScopeResponse
DataScopeResponse.description:
The caller's row-level scope, as the policy layer resolved it.

``workspace_ids`` is part of the wire format because ``DataScope`` carries
it and clients need it: it answers "which workspaces may I target" without a
second request, and it is what ``scope_filter`` actually applies for a plain
user. Omitting it here meant the value was computed, returned by
``to_dict()``, and then quietly dropped on the floor by Pydantic.

GroupKind.title: GroupKind
GroupKind.description: A lab group owns workspaces; the public group is the shared fallback.

GroupMemberRead.title: GroupMemberRead
GroupMemberRead.description: A member row — the user summary plus their standing in this group.

GroupMembership.title: GroupMembership
GroupMembership.description: One of the caller's memberships, including their role inside the group.

GroupSyncRequest.title: GroupSyncRequest
GroupSyncRequest.description:
Ask the backend to refresh memberships from the directory.

``dry_run`` reports what would change without writing anything.

IdeAccess.title: IdeAccess
IdeAccess.description: A short-lived, signed URL for an instance's web IDE.

IdeType.title: IdeType
IdeType.description: Which web IDE an instance exposes through the ingress, if any.

ImageDetail.title: ImageDetail
ImageDetail.description: The same entry with the history behind it.

ImageKind.title: ImageKind
ImageKind.description:
Where an image stands in the catalogue.

``PERSONAL`` images belong to one user and are pushed by them;
``OFFICIAL`` ones are curated by an administrator and are what the picker
offers by default; ``SHARED`` covers a group's agreed images.

ImageRegister.title: ImageRegister
ImageRegister.description: Add one reference to the catalogue.

ImageSummary.title: ImageSummary
ImageSummary.description: One catalogue entry, as the picker and the list page need it.

ImageUsage.title: ImageUsage
ImageUsage.description: Totals for the header of the images page.

ImageVisibility.title: ImageVisibility
ImageVisibility.description:
Who may *see* an image in the catalogue.

Distinct from :class:`~app.models.enums.ApplicationVisibility` only in
audience; the same four steps apply, and the same rule holds: visibility
governs reads, not ownership.

InstanceAction.title: InstanceAction
InstanceAction.description: Optional body for start/stop, so the reason lands in the audit trail.

InstanceDetail.title: InstanceDetail
InstanceDetail.description: Adds everything needed to actually connect to the instance.

InstanceStatus.title: InstanceStatus
InstanceStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a container instance.

Mirrors what the UI shows, not the Kubernetes phase: ``PENDING`` is "accepted
but nothing applied yet", ``CREATING`` is "objects applied, waiting for the
pod", and ``RUNNING`` is "the pod is up". Collapsing those would leave a user
staring at a spinner with no idea which half is stuck.

InstanceSummary.title: InstanceSummary
InstanceSummary.description: One row of the instance list.

MonitorDashboardRead.title: MonitorDashboardRead
MonitorDashboardRead.description: One dashboard the caller may open.

MonitorEmbedRead.title: MonitorEmbedRead
MonitorEmbedRead.description:
A freshly minted, scope-locked Grafana URL.

Short-lived by construction: the URL carries the scope, so it is re-minted
every time the page needs one rather than handed out once and cached.

MonitorInventory.title: MonitorInventory
MonitorInventory.description: The platform's own view of the cluster. Not tenant-scoped.

MonitorOverview.title: MonitorOverview
MonitorOverview.description:
Everything the monitoring page needs on first paint.

One response rather than four round-trips, because four requests that can
disagree with each other produce a page that describes two different moments.

MonitorScopeRead.title: MonitorScopeRead
MonitorScopeRead.description:
What the caller's monitoring is currently limited to.

Returned to the page so the filter is visible rather than implied. A user
looking at a flat line deserves to know whether it is flat because nothing is
happening or because they are filtered to a namespace with nothing in it.

NetworkType.title: NetworkType
NetworkType.description:
Egress posture of a workspace namespace.

Every workspace starts from default-deny; this widens it deliberately.

PermissionCatalogue.title: PermissionCatalogue
PermissionCatalogue.description: Every permission code, grouped by category — drives the UI matrix.

PermissionsResponse.title: PermissionsResponse
PermissionsResponse.description:
The complete authorisation state for the caller.

The frontend uses this purely to decide what to render; the backend remains
the only enforcement point.

ProviderInfo.title: ProviderInfo
ProviderInfo.description: Which login methods the UI should offer.

RefreshRequest.title: RefreshRequest
RefreshRequest.description:
The refresh token normally arrives as an httpOnly cookie.

The body field exists for non-browser clients that cannot use cookies.

ResourceGroupKind.title: ResourceGroupKind
ResourceGroupKind.description:
Who may use a resource group.

``PUBLIC`` groups are offered to every workspace; ``PRIVATE`` groups must be
granted explicitly (plan §5.2) — that grant is the *only* binding between a
tenant and a pool of hardware.

RoleScope.title: RoleScope
RoleScope.description:
Where a role assignment applies.

``GROUP`` scoped assignments carry a ``group_id`` — this is what makes
``group_admin`` inherently limited to one group.

StorageDetail.title: StorageDetail
StorageDetail.description: A volume plus its cluster coordinates.

StorageKind.title: StorageKind
StorageKind.description:
What a volume is *for*. The kind decides who may own it and how it mounts.

This is not cosmetic taxonomy. A ``dataset`` is read-only everywhere it
appears — enforced at the mount, not merely in the UI — because the one
thing worse than an unreadable dataset is a dataset that a training job
silently overwrote. ``PERSONAL_HOME`` is the volume that makes an instance
disposable: it is what survives when the container is deleted.

StorageResize.title: StorageResize
StorageResize.description:
Grow a volume.

Only the target size is accepted. There is no `shrink` flag, because
Kubernetes cannot do it and offering the option would produce a form that
fails on submit.

StorageStatus.title: StorageStatus
StorageStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a volume.

``PENDING`` and ``BOUND`` mirror the PersistentVolumeClaim phases rather
than inventing a parallel vocabulary, so an operator reading
``kubectl get pvc`` and the UI see the same word.

StorageSummary.title: StorageSummary
StorageSummary.description: One row of the storage list.

TaskDetail.title: TaskDetail
TaskDetail.description: The task list row plus everything only the detail view needs.

TaskStatus.title: TaskStatus
TaskStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a one-shot task (a Kubernetes Job).

``TIMEOUT`` is kept apart from ``FAILED``: hitting your own runtime limit is
a different problem from your code returning non-zero, and the fix is
different too.

TaskSummary.title: TaskSummary
TaskSummary.description: One row of the task list.

TaskUpdate.title: TaskUpdate
TaskUpdate.description: Only the fields that can honestly change after submission.

TokenResponse.title: TokenResponse
TokenResponse.description:
Issued on login and on every refresh.

``expires_in`` is what the frontend schedules its silent refresh against.

UsageBreakdownRowRead.title: UsageBreakdownRowRead
UsageBreakdownRowRead.description: One bucket of a grouped report.

UsageDayRead.title: UsageDayRead
UsageDayRead.description: One day of the time series. Days with no usage are present, with zeros.

UsageKind.title: UsageKind
UsageKind.description:
Which kind of workload consumed the resources.

Deliberately narrower than :class:`WorkloadKind`. That enum also covers
workspaces, applications, storages and images, none of which hold a
accelerator for any length of time — letting those values into a usage row
would invite summing a column that can never legitimately be non-zero.

UsageKindRead.title: UsageKindRead
UsageKindRead.description: The workload kinds a usage row can carry, for the filter control.

UsageMetaRead.title: UsageMetaRead
UsageMetaRead.description:
What the client needs in order to build the filter controls.

Sent rather than hard-coded in the frontend so the two cannot drift: adding a
breakdown dimension should light up in the UI without a second commit.

UsageSummaryRead.title: UsageSummaryRead
UsageSummaryRead.description: What the usage centre shows above the charts.

UsageTotalsRead.description: Aggregated consumption over some window or bucket.

UserCreate.title: UserCreate
UserCreate.description:
Create a local account.

Directory-backed users are created automatically on first login; this
endpoint exists for the break-glass accounts an administrator must be able
to issue without the directory being reachable.

UserGroupsUpdate.title: UserGroupsUpdate
UserGroupsUpdate.description:
Replace the user's group memberships.

``primary_group_id`` must be one of ``group_ids``; membership flags for
directory-managed rows are preserved by the service.

UserRoleGrant.title: UserRoleGrant
UserRoleGrant.description: Grant a role globally or within one group.

UserSelfUpdate.title: UserSelfUpdate
UserSelfUpdate.description: What a user may change about themselves.

UserSummary.title: UserSummary
UserSummary.description: A row in the user list.

UserUpdate.title: UserUpdate
UserUpdate.description: Partial update; only the fields present are applied.

WatchedContainer.title: WatchedContainer
WatchedContainer.description: A live instance the caller may watch, with the names Grafana filters on.

WorkloadEventRead.title: WorkloadEventRead
WorkloadEventRead.description: One entry of the workload timeline.

WorkspaceMemberAssign.title: WorkspaceMemberAssign
WorkspaceMemberAssign.description:
Assign a user to a workspace.

Because a user may belong to exactly one workspace, this *moves* them if
they already have one — which is why the payload requires an explicit
acknowledgement rather than silently relocating someone's work.

WorkspaceQuotaSync.title: WorkspaceQuotaSync
WorkspaceQuotaSync.description: Result of recomputing a workspace's quota and pushing it to the cluster.

WorkspaceRef.title: WorkspaceRef
WorkspaceRef.description:
The single workspace a user belongs to (plan D7).

Populated from Phase 2 onwards; ``None`` until then.

WorkspaceRole.title: WorkspaceRole
WorkspaceRole.description:
A user's standing inside a workspace.

Distinct from :class:`GroupRole`: administering a lab does not automatically
give you the right to delete someone's workspace, and a workspace owner is
not thereby a group admin.

WorkspaceStatus.title: WorkspaceStatus
WorkspaceStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a workspace.

A workspace is only ``ACTIVE`` once its Kubernetes namespace, quota and
network policy all exist; ``ERROR`` means provisioning half-finished and the
reconcile loop will retry.
